speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The history of a recent camping trip in Minnesota, combined with self-resolving joint pain and now wrist pain with fever, strongly raises concern for Lyme disease. Before we proceed, did you notice any rash, specifically one that looked like a bull's-eye or target lesion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma Gangrenosum secondary to Pseudomonas sepsis. The clinical picture of fever, chills, violaceous necrotic lesions on the hands/wrists, and severe wrist pain/swelling is characteristic of Pseudomonas infection, likely introduced via a traumatic injury during the camping trip, rather than Lyme disease.
